title: Averaged indicator as Gaussian measure
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in\mathbb R^n$. Then
\[
u_\theta(x)=\gamma_n\bigl(\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y\in A\}\bigr),
\]
where $u_\theta(x)=\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ and $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable, then $u_\theta(x)=\gamma_n\{y:\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y\in A\}$ for every real $\theta$ and every $x$.
